Don't buy any mid cap before you check these three numbers.
Return on equity above fifteen percent. Promoters owning more than half. And low debt. Most mid caps fail. These six pass.
One. Abbott India. Medicines like Thyronorm and Digene. Return on equity, thirty four percent. Promoters own seventy five percent.
Two. Nippon Life AMC. It runs mutual funds. Return on equity, thirty four percent. And Indian funds raised their stake from thirteen to fifteen and a half percent.
Three. Oracle Financial Services. Software that runs banks around the world. Thirty three percent return on equity, almost no debt, and a four percent dividend.
Four. Colgate India. Yes, your toothpaste. Return on equity, eighty three percent. The catch? Sales grow only five percent a year.
Five. Mazagon Dock. It builds the Navy's submarines and warships. Profit grew thirty three percent a year for five years, and the government owns eighty one percent.
Six. Coromandel International, from Chennai. Fertilisers for India's farmers. Indian funds raised their stake from sixteen to twenty and a half percent.
But strong doesn't mean cheap. All six trade at twenty four to thirty four times their earnings.
